effort: Read a likely passing lane before release and move through an oblique plant.
brief: Extend commitment reading to anticipation of an intended lane. E1 briefly removes the final ball-flight information, so the athlete must use preparatory body cues. The rest of the class supplies alternating forward transfer, same-leg lateral acceptance, quarter-turn coordination, single-support vertical extension and curved approach force. These are general opponent cues, not sport-specific tactical mastery.
anchor_protocol: Coach preselects a left/right low pass (two each). Athlete sees a natural step and trunk/arm preparation; coach briefly freezes before releasing. Athlete predicts the likely lane and moves 1.5 m diagonally toward their own projected gate on a separate path. Coach then completes the low roll/pass on the ball path, allowing prediction to be checked. Athlete stops within 2 m; never touches the ball. No spoken direction and no deliberately inconsistent decoy cues yet. With uncertain readiness, show a more complete, slower preparation before freezing rather than adding trials.
quality_marker: E1: four predicted lanes, scored correct/incorrect against the coach’s preselected release, plus plant/stop control. Record where the motion was frozen; scores from different freeze points are not directly comparable. Movement before any useful body information is guessing, not anticipation.
layout: Require a measured combined bay up to 10 m long × 7 m wide, with separate ball/athlete paths and ≥2 m clearance. Athlete branch travel starts at 2 m, extends 1.5 m diagonally, with 2 m stopping buffers; coach never rolls into an athlete route. E6 uses a gentle 4 m arc within an up-to-10 m × 7 m area, including 2 m tangent stopping space; it is not a tight circle or full-speed curve. Bounds use short individualized distances inside the remaining clear strip. No additional runway is assumed. Full-route width is a requirement, not confirmed inventory: branch stopping extensions can exceed a 4 m bay. Compact same-drill option: use 1 m E1 diagonal routes plus 1 m stopping, preserving the pre-release prediction and four trials; total E1 movement 4 m plus up to 4 m stopping. Use a gentle E6 arc of 2 m with 2 m tangent stopping in a verified 4 m-wide bay (four runs, 8 m movement plus up to 8 m stopping). Keep speed controlled and record route changes; no comparison with the longer route is implied. At setup, mark complete body/landing envelopes, both possible routes, run-off and the coach position; a floor-line diagram alone does not establish clearance. If even the compact footprint is unavailable, resolve the layout before delivery.
progression: Previous: Class 6 prescribed an early closeout read, controlled bilateral landing and four unilateral rebound contacts; no feedback supplied. Current: pre-release inference and six modest unilateral landings distributed over three distinct tasks, with four bilateral turns. Do not add distance to those landings. Retain lateral/hinge/ankle strength and reduce secondary compound sets. Advance only when actual prediction/control and landing quality are reported without lost recovery; otherwise expose more cue information and shorten the force tasks.
audit: Pass preparation before release is distinct from reading release direction in Class 3 and arrival time in Class 6. Unilateral work was capped at two contacts per supporting drill instead of multiple bounding sets. Curved running is short and controlled, not maximum-velocity training. No strength load increase is prescribed. Next class adds a second decision only through a clear, short movement problem. Full-sequence revision: replaced the ambiguous crossover bound, which overlapped too closely with the earlier skater bound, with a clearly defined single-leg vertical hop. Landing count is unchanged; no forced crossed-knee landing is prescribed. Geometry revision: removed the implication that every full-length angled route fits a 4 m-wide rectangle; added a quantified shorter same-drill alternative. Default ledger totals remain the full-route prescription; compact actual travel is logged separately.

explosive.name: Pre-Release Pass-Lane Prediction
explosive.job: Main anticipation task: infer an intended pass lane from body preparation before ball flight makes the answer obvious.
explosive.execution: Coach freezes the preparation, athlete selects a 1.5 m diagonal gate, coach completes the preselected low release on the separate path; stop within 2 m. Rest 75 s between trials, 90 s before E2. Reveal more preparation if guesses dominate.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Alternating Forward Bounds
explosive.job: Transfer forward impulse from leg to leg without the same-leg landing used in earlier forward hops.
explosive.execution: Start from a short walking setup; bound left-to-right then right-to-left, one landing per leg, finish controlled. Do not seek maximal stride length. Rest 90 s before E3; shorten travel if pelvis drops or contact gets loud.

explosive.name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop to Stick
explosive.job: Own a lateral landing back on the same leg, a different support demand from skater bounds.
explosive.execution: Hop a small distance outward on the right leg and land right; repeat on the left after 45 s. Hold 2 s; rest 60 s before E4. Shorten distance for extra hopping or knee drift.

explosive.name: 90-Degree Jump Turn to Stick
explosive.job: Reorient feet/hips together while airborne, then establish a usable two-foot base toward the chosen lane.
explosive.execution: Low two-foot jump with a quarter turn, both feet land and hold 2 s. Rotate through the whole body, not a fixed planted knee. Rest 30 s between jumps and 60 s before E5. Reduce turn angle if alignment is lost.

explosive.name: Single-Leg Vertical Hop to Stick
explosive.job: Express vertical extension from a single support without a crossing reach, keeping the body available to redirect from an anticipated lane.
explosive.execution: Make one small vertical hop on the same leg, land under the hip and hold 2 s. Repeat the other leg after 60 s; rest 60 s before E6. Lower height for pelvic drop or an extra hop.

explosive.name: Inside-Arc Acceleration
explosive.job: Apply continuous inward force over a gentle curved path rather than a single sharp plant.
explosive.execution: Run a marked gentle arc for 4 m at controlled acceleration effort, then stop within 2 m along its tangent. Lean as a whole body; no foot crossing. Rest 60 s between runs and 90 s before strength. Widen/slow the arc for unstable footing.

stabilization.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press — light band
stabilization.job: Light resistance to trunk rotation while choosing an oblique line.
stabilization.execution: Coach supplies a steady sideways band pull at chest height while athlete half-kneels and presses forward without rotating. Use comfortable knee contact; use standing split stance instead if kneeling is unsuitable. Reduce tension if trunk turns. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

stabilization.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — light
stabilization.job: Keep the lateral foot contact controlled under angled push-off.
stabilization.execution: With heel supported and shin still, turn the forefoot slightly outward against a light band held securely by the coach, away from the face. Return slowly; no ankle rolling or knee turn. Reduce tension/range for loss of control. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

primary.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
primary.job: Retain the step-out-and-return strength anchor for moving into an interception lane.
primary.execution: Step sideways from standing, sit into the working hip with whole-foot pressure, then return to the starting stance. Reduce depth/load for groin discomfort, knee collapse or twisting. Rest 90 s between sides; 120 s between rounds and 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Split Squat — dumbbells at sides
primary.job: Stable lead-leg extension to leave the anticipated route position.
primary.execution: Keep both feet on the floor in a stationary staggered stance; front heel down, controlled descent, drive through the lead leg. Reduce depth/load for pelvic rotation or rear-leg jumping. Rest 90 s between sides; 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
primary.job: Hip force and trunk control during the oblique plant without another long hinge block.
primary.execution: Hinge from standing with soft knees; keep weights close and stop descent where the pelvis/spine remain controlled. Finish tall without leaning back. Reduce range/load for rounding. Rest 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Partner Manual-Resistance Hamstring Curl
primary.job: Knee-flexor contribution during curved running, held at a controlled support dose.
primary.execution: Lie prone on a comfortable floor surface; coach applies smooth resistance above the heel while the athlete bends and straightens the knee through an owned range. Keep hips down; no sudden pushes. Match resistance to 2–3 RIR, not a contest. If prone support/contact is unsuitable, use Seated Band Hamstring Curl instead, same sets/reps per side: sit on a stable bench, secure a light band at the heel with a coach holding steady forward tension, then pull the heel beneath the bench without moving the thigh. Qualify band/bench fit; no sudden release. This replaces only this slot and preserves totals. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise — supported standing, dumbbell
primary.job: Single-leg ankle drive as the interception path lengthens.
primary.execution: Stand on flat floor with a nearly straight knee and light hand support; raise the heel, pause briefly and lower for 2 seconds. No bounce or ankle roll. Reduce load when heel height declines. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, bent-knee
primary.job: Bent-knee ankle force in the initial low intercept stance.
primary.execution: Use a stable bench, knees near right angles, secure dumbbells on distal thighs above knees. Lower heels for 2 seconds to the floor, pause, then rise. Reduce load for bouncing or shortened range. Rest 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.
